A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ParaReval study, with matching authors, experimental design, and extensive corresponding results. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the main text and complete appendices despite v4's French translation and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original human annotations of 1,548 revision pairs, evaluations of six revision models, and analyses of automatic metrics' agreement with human judgments.

after.justification: v4 retains these original annotation and evaluation results, including detailed appendix analyses, while revising several reported agreement scores.

M1.justification: LLM-Choice and LLM-Likert become GML-Choix and GML-Likert, but retain their pairwise-choice and individual-scoring procedures, reference conditions, and substantive prompts. No new algorithm, model component, or training objective is introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ParaRev evaluation data: 258 paragraph pairs with two instructions each, covering the same rewriting, concision, and content-deletion categories. Translating the paper into French does not introduce French-language evaluation data or a new task.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same six revision models, no-edits control, similarity metrics, BETS, BLANC, ParaPLUIE, LLM judges, and random baseline. The appendix also retains both Mistral and Llama-based ParaPLUIE comparisons; translated names do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: The stated protocol retains 516 revision inputs per model, 1,548 annotated pairs, 10 annotators, balanced model comparisons, and the same agreement measures. Difficulty groups remain 530 easy, 214 medium, and 575 hard pairs. No changed scoring definition or experimental setting is documented to explain the revised scores.

E4.justification: Existing diagnostic analyses receive revised quantitative evidence without adding new analysis questions. For example, the reference ablation changes Choice's without/with-reference accuracy from 0.496/0.494 in v1 Section 6.3 to 0.564/0.563 in v4 Appendix J. Category and difficulty plots are also revised; self-preference, tie-distribution, and edit-distance analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging three runs except for GPT-4o, limited to one run, and use the same 129 doubly annotated pairs for inter-annotator agreement. Neither adds confidence intervals, significance tests, or a new uncertainty-reporting practice. Changed agreement coefficients are result revisions.

E6.justification: The central agreement results are substantially revised. From v1 Table 5 to v4 Table 4, pairwise accuracy changes from 0.496 to 0.564 for Choice, 0.338 to 0.436 for Likert, and 0.477 to 0.551 for ParaPLUIE. Choice replaces Likert as the highest-Cramer's-V method, and category/difficulty plots also change. Revision-model scores and human-preference counts remain unchanged; the PDFs do not explain the numerical revisions.

T1.justification: The definitions of extended preference and difficulty categories retain their meaning. Neither version contains a theoretical development or proof that is added, removed, or substantively revised in the other.

C1.justification: The abstracts, contributions, and conclusions retain the same scientific claims: similarity metrics inadequately assess revision quality, LLM judges handle instruction following better than correctness, and complementary metrics offer a practical hybrid evaluation. The ParaReval contribution and reference-free evaluation claim remain.

C2.justification: For difficult cases, v1 Section 6.2 describes ParaPLUIE as preventing revision-model hallucinations; v4 Section 6 instead describes detecting possible hallucinations. This modestly narrows the mechanism claim. The substantive limitations and other interpretations are retained, including those moved to Appendix M.

D1.justification: Both versions provide equivalent revision and judging prompts, the same repository link, and the same resource disclosures: approximately 12 RTX 2080 hours, 249 V100/A100 hours, and $29.01 in GPT API credits. Relocating these disclosures to appendices does not add reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v4 removes the explicit MoverScore and SemDist discussion and their corresponding references, while adding several TALN bibliography entries, including Laignelet and Rioult (2009). These are limited coverage changes; the positioning relative to prior revision evaluation and LLM-judge research remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The paper is extensively translated into French, with bilingual abstracts and translated terminology throughout. Numbered subsections become paragraph headings, while the taxonomy, category-specific annotation questions, reference-impact discussion, limitations, and ethics material are reorganized between the main text and appendices.

P2.justification: v4 replaces the two-column main layout with a smaller-page, predominantly single-column layout using wrapped figures and tables. Figures receive translated labels, modified markers and icons, and revised axes; tables and prompt boxes are reformatted. The taxonomy table and illustrative SARI case move to appendices without removing their content.

improvement.justification: The scientific scope is preserved, and the hallucination-detection wording is more restrained. However, v4 introduces an unexplained reporting inconsistency: Table 4 gives GLEU Cramer's V as 0.193, while Appendix L Figure 16 plots its overall value near 0.11; v1 Table 5 and Appendix I Figure 17 agree near 0.19. This weakens verification of the metric comparison and outweighs the limited clarification and presentation benefits.
